[Judgment of the Court was made by MRS.V.BHAVANI SUBBAROYAN.J.] CMP(MD)No.1657 of 2024 in CMA(MD)SR.No.53941 of 2023 is filed to condone the delay of 417 days in filing the appeal against the judgment and decree dated 22.10.2021 made in Ar.O.P.No.02 of 2017.

2. The 1st respondent herein is the claimant whose lands measuring an extent of 498.616 cents comprised in Survey Nos.583, 591, https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis and 584, 590/1 and 593 situate at Veerapandi Village, Theni Taluk, Theni District, were acquired by the 2nd respondent herein/competent authority for land acquisition, for formation of National Highways.
The appellant is the beneficiary of the National Highways.

The competent authority fixed the value of the land at Rs.15,379/- per cent and along with 10% appreciation value, has awarded a total compensation of Rs.29,80,509/- for 498.616 cents of the 1st respondent.

The 1st respondent received the said compensation amount under protest and thereafter filed an appeal before the District Collector/Arbitrator, Theni, contending that even before the acquisition proceedings, his adjacent lands were converted as house sites and sold for higher value.
However, the District Collector/Arbitrator, Theni, dismissed the appeal confirming the award passed by the 2nd respondent/competent authority.
Aggrieved by the same, the 1st respondents/claimant filed Arbitration Original Petition No. 02/2017 before the learned Principal District Judge, Theni.
In the said Ar.O.P., the 1st respondent examined himself as PW1 and marked six documents.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis and 3.

Before the Court below, the 1st respondent/claimant contended that the District Collector/Arbitrator, Theni, has erroneously rejected Ex.P5-sale deed dated 12.01.2010 relied upon by the 1st respondent to prove that his adjacent lands were sold for a sufficiently higher value, on the ground that the acquired lands of the 1st respondent were classified as 'dry' in the revenue records The Project Director vs P.Rajaguru on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102273895/
2 and therefore, Ex.P5 cannot be applied to his lands.
According to the 1 st respondent, the Arbitrator totally ignored the fact that the distance between Ex.P5 sale deed lands and the aquired lands of the 1st respondent is only about 1 kilometre.

The learned Judge, finding that the nature of the lands covered under Ex.P5 is a vacant dry land as that of the 1st respondent's lands and that the said sale deed was not disputed/questioned by the compentent authority and the District Collector, Theni District, nor they have produced any supporting documents to substantiate their fixation of market value, by order dated 22.10.2021 in Ar.O.P.No.02 of 2017, has enhanced the compensation to Rs.4,36,80,062/- as against a sum of Rs.29,80,509/- awarded by the 2 nd respondent and confirmed by the District Collector / Arbitrator, Theni.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis and
As against the said order, the appellant has filed this appeal with the delay of 417 days.
4. As regards the delay of 417 days in filing this appeal, learned counsel for the appellant referred to paragraph 14 of the affidavit which relates to usual file-pushing and administrative exigency.

5. On the merits of the case, it is the main bone of contention of the learned counsel for the appellant that it is a well settled law that reappraisal of evidence by the Court under Section 34 of the Arbitration & Conciliation Act, 1996, is not permissible and therefore, the Court below ought not to have examined as to whether the reasons recorded by the compentent authority are right or erroneous.

He further submitted that as per Section 34(2) of the Act, the learned Judge has limited powers and can set aside the arbitral award only on the grounds namely, incapacity of party,
invalidity of agreement, notice not given to party, unable to present case and award beyond scope of reference.

However, in the present case, the Court below bent upon to examine the reasons https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis and recorded by the competent authority ignoring its limited powers conferred under Section 32(2) and therefore, the impugned order is liable to be set aside.

Learned counsel also contended that it would not be open for the Court below in the proceedings under Section 34 of the Act, to modify the award and the appropriate course to be adoped is to set aside the award and remit the matter to the Arbitrator in terms of Section 34(4) for fresh adjudication.

In support of the said proposition, learned counsel relied on the following decisions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court:-
(i) National Highways Authority of India vs. Sri P.Nagaraju @ Cheluvaiah and another [C.A.No.4671 of 2022, dated 11.07.2022]
(ii) Project Director, National Highways Authority of India vs. M.Hakeem and another reported in 2021 SCC Online SC 473.
6.

sentences.text: Given the object sought to be achieved under both the Arbitration Act and the Commercial Courts Act, that is, the speedy resolution of disputes, the expression sufficient cause is not elastic enough to cover long delays beyond the period provided by the appeal provision itself.
Besides, the expression sufficient cause is not itself a loose panacea for the ill of pressing negligent and stale claims.

This Court,
in Basawaraj v. Land Acquisition Officer, (2013) 14 SCC 81, has held:
9. Sufficient cause is the cause for which the defendant could not be blamed for his absence.

entities.text: Basawaraj v. Land Acquisition Officer, (2013) 14 SCC 81
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The meaning of the word sufficient is adequate or enough, inasmuch as may be necessary to answer the purpose intended.

Therefore, the word sufficient embraces no more than that which provides a platitude, which when the act done suffices to accomplish the purpose intended in the facts and circumstances existing in a case, duly examined from the viewpoint of a reasonable standard of a cautious man.

In this context, sufficient cause means that the party should not have acted in a negligent manner or there was a want of bona fide on its part in view of the facts and circumstances of a case or it cannot be alleged that the party has not acted diligently or remained inactive.

However, the facts and circumstances of each case must afford sufficient ground to https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis and enable the court concerned to exercise discretion for the reason that whenever the court exercises discretion, it has to be exercised judiciously.

The applicant must satisfy the court that he was prevented by any sufficient cause from prosecuting his case, and unless a satisfactory explanation is furnished, the court should not allow the application for condonation of delay.
The court has to examine whether the mistake is bona fide or was merely a device to cover an ulterior purpose.

(See Manindra Land and Building Corpn. Ltd. v. Bhutnath Banerjee [AIR 1964 SC 1336] , Mata Din v. A.
Narayanan [(1969) 2 SCC 770 : AIR 1970 SC 1953] , Parimal v. Veena [(2011) 3 SCC 545 : (2011) 2 SCC (Civ) 1 : AIR 2011 SC 1150] and Maniben Devraj Shah v.
Municipal Corpn. of Brihan Mumbai [(2012) 5 SCC 157 : (2012) 3 SCC (Civ) 24 : AIR 2012 SC 1629]
.)
10.

The expression sufficient cause should be given a liberal interpretation to ensure that substantial justice is done, but only so long as negligence, inaction or lack of bona fides cannot be imputed to the party concerned, whether or not sufficient cause has been furnished, can be decided on the facts of a particular case and no straitjacket formula is possible.

sentences.text:
While dealing with the appeals filed under Section 37 of the Arbitration & Conciliation Act, 1996 with the delay, the Apex in the very same judgment has held as follows:-
''63.

Given the aforesaid and the object of speedy disposal sought to be achieved both under the Arbitration Act and the Commercial Courts Act, for appeals filed under section 37 of the Arbitration Act that are governed by Articles 116 and 117 of the Limitation Act or section 13(1A) of the Commercial Courts Act, a delay beyond 90 days, 30 days or 60 days, respectively, is to be condoned by way of exception and not by way of rule.

In a fit case in which a party has otherwise acted bona fide and not in a negligent manner, a short delay beyond such period can, in the discretion of the court, be condoned, always bearing in mind that the other side of the picture is that the opposite party may have acquired both in equity and justice, what may now be lost by the first partys inaction, negligence or laches.''

9. In Borse Brothers Engineers and Contractors Private Limited's case [cited supra], though there was 75 days delay beyond the period of 60 days provided by the Commercial Courts Act, the Apex Court declined to condone the delay, and held as follows:-
''65.

entities.text: Borse Brothers Engineers and Contractors Private Limited
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Apart from this, there is a long delay of 131 days beyond the 60- day period provided for filing an appeal https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis and under section 13(1A) of the Commercial Courts Act.
There is no explanation worth the name contained in the condonation of delay application, beyond the usual file-pushing and administrative exigency.
This appeal is therefore dismissed.
67. That apart, on the facts of this appeal, there is a long delay of 75 days beyond the period of 60 days provided by the Commercial Courts Act.

Despite the fact that a certified copy of the District Courts judgment was obtained by the respondent on 27.04.2019, the appeal was filed only on 09.09.2019, the explanation for delay being:
2. That, the certified copy of the order dated 01/04/2013 was received by the appellant on 27/04/2019.
Thereafter the matter was placed before the CGM purchase MPPKVVCL for the compliance of the order.
The same was then sent to the law officer, MPPKVVCL for opinion.
3. That after taking opinion for appeal, and approval of the concerned authorities, the officer-in-charge was appointed vide order dated 23/07/2019.

4. That, thereafter due to bulky records of the case and for procurement of the necessary documents some delay has been caused however, the appeal has been prepared and filed to pursuant to the same and further delay.

5. That due to the aforesaid procedural approval and since the appellant is a public entity formed under the Energy department of the State Government, the delay caused in filing the appeal is bonafide and which deserve[s] to be condoned.

The Project Director vs P.Rajaguru on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102273895/
5 68.
This explanation falls woefully short of making out any sufficient cause.
This appeal is therefore allowed and the condonation of delay is set aside on this score also.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis and 69.
In the Civil Appeal arising out of SLP (C) Diary No. 18079 of 2020, there is a huge delay of 227 days in filing the appeal, and a 200-day delay in refiling.
The facts of this case also show that there was no sufficient cause whatsoever to condone such a long delay.
The impugned judgment of the High Court of Delhi dated 15.10.2019 cannot be faulted on this score and this appeal is consequently dismissed.''

10. Reverting to the case on hand, with regard to condonation of 417 days delay in filing this appeal,
the appellant has assigned the following reason at paragraph 14 which reads as follows:-
''14.

I humbly submit that the Learned District judge made the order on 22.10.2021 and copy was made ready on 09.06.2023 and the present Appeal under section 37 of the act ought to have been filed within 90 days from thereon copy was made ready on 09.06.202 on 22.10.2021 and within 90 days from thereon.
Inadvertently, there is delay in filing the present CMA.

Initially, this project was dealt by PIU,
Madurai therefore the files relating to the court case was with the PIU, Madurai and a new PIU was formed at Dindigul on 22.01.2018 earlier.
The files relating to PIU, Dindigul was received from the existing PIU, Madurai and there was some delay in receiving the files.

Moreover, the newly formed PIU, Dindigul was functioned without full time Project Director from 22.01.2018 to 01.09.2020 and during that time an incharge Project Director, Nagercoil was functioning with additional charge.
Simultaneously, the Regional officer, Madurai of NHAI was also vacant from 26.04.2019 to 23.08.2021.

Moreover, the Hon'bie https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis and Supreme Court's suo moto orders in extending limitation due to COVID-19 made in suo Moto Writ (Civil) No. 3 of 2020 vide order dated 23.03.2020, 08.03.2021 and 23.09.2021 and order dated 10.01.2022 to exclude the period from 15.03.2020 till 28.02.2022 for computing limitation in filing suit, appeal, application or proceedings in judicial and quasi judicial forum.

Therefore, the delay may be condoned for the above stated reasons.''
11.
Perusal of the said extracted portion reveals that usual file- pushing and administrative exigency are cited as reasons for the delay.

Though in Borse Brothers Engineers and Contractors Private Limited's case, the Apex Court held that in a fit case, in which, a party has otherwise acted bona fide and not in a negligent manner, a short delay beyond such period can, in the discretion of the court,
be condoned by way of exception, always bearing in mind the other side of the picture, in the case on hand, while the impugned order is dated 22.10.2021, the copy application itself was made belatedly on 01.06.2023.

Though the Apex Court extended the limitation period due to Covid-19 for the cases where the limitation would have expired during the period between 15.03.2020 till 28.02.2022,
even thereafter, the appellant has not acted promptly and made copy application only on 01.06.2023 after a lapse of one year and https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis and three months from 28.02.2022,
The Project Director vs P.Rajaguru on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102273895/
6 for which, usual file-pushing and administrative exigency are cited as reasons.

sentences.text: The said reason itself shows that the appellant acted in a negligent manner and therefore, keeping in mind the other side of the picture i.e., despite the acquisition proceedings initiated in the year 2010, award was passed in 2012 and award was enhanced in 2021, till date, the 1st respondent is not able to receive the enhanced compensation, this Court is of the considered opinion that neither there is pleading of exceptional circumstances by the appellant nor there is acceptable reason furnished to condone the delay by way of exception.
Hence, this Court is not inclined to condone the delay.
12. Accordingly, the delay condonation petition in CMP(MD)No.1657 of 2024 is dismissed.
Consequently, CMA(MD)SR.No.53941 of 2023 is rejected.
